result.summary: This part of the anthropic-sdk-go root package holds generated API types and service methods for beta endpoints: agents, deployments, dreams, environments, files and memory stores. Each method sends caller-supplied parameters over HTTP to the configured Anthropic API. I checked the init functions, the request construction and the use of headers and paths, and found no hidden network destinations, credential harvesting, code execution or persistence.

findings.title: Generated SDK code with no suspicious behavior
findings.detail: All files are Stainless-generated API client code: typed request/response structs, union helpers, and service methods that send HTTP requests to the configured Anthropic API endpoint through internal/requestconfig. The init() functions only call apijson.RegisterUnion with constant discriminators. There is no file, environment or credential access beyond what the caller passes in, no exec, and no hidden endpoints.

capabilities.explanation: Every service method (e.g. BetaAgentService.New/Get/List, BetaDeploymentService.Run, BetaFileService.Upload/Download, BetaMemoryStoreMemoryService.*) builds a path such as "v1/agents?beta=true" and calls requestconfig.ExecuteNewRequest or cfg.Execute, which performs HTTP requests to the Anthropic API base URL set in the client options. This is the SDK's whole purpose.

Comes from the reflection-based serialization machinery the generated types use: apijson.UnmarshalRoot, param.MarshalObject/MarshalUnion, and apijson.RegisterUnion called in init() to register discriminated unions, plus RequestOptionFunc closures run by requestconfig. None of this loads or runs code chosen at run time from outside the program; the init functions only register type discriminators.

data_flows.what: Caller-supplied agent definitions (name, system prompt, tools, MCP server URLs, metadata), workspace ID and beta headers
Deployment configs including initial events, resources such as GitHub repository authorization tokens supplied by the caller, vault IDs, schedules
File contents the caller uploads as multipart form data; file downloads returned to the caller as an http.Response
Memory text content and paths supplied by the caller
Worker poll/heartbeat/ack/stop requests, including an optional Anthropic-Worker-ID header
